sovereign_country.strategic_role: 12.5%统一企业税、CySEC外汇券商牌照与游戏发行业务

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Lightweight Ad-Monetized Mobile Games

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Cyprus (unitary national jurisdiction; no fiscally distinct sub-state territories)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statuate_and_sections: Companies Law, Cap. 113 (Republic of Cyprus), Sections 3, 5, 18, 20 and Schedule 1 (Table A)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver, Nicosia, Cyprus
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form HE1 – Application for Registration of a Private Company as a Limited Company, together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a private limited company under Cyprus Companies Law Cap. 113; shares may be issued at par or premium and consideration may be satisfied by cash or in-kind, without any statutory escrow obligation for this non-regulated activity
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the incorporation of the Company, as set out in the Memorandum and Articles of Association, be ratified and accepted. RESOLVED: That the subscribers hereby approve the allotment of the initial issued share capital to the subscribers at par and the directors are authorised to issue share certificates accordingly. RESOLVED: That the registered office of the Company be fixed at [address], Nicosia, Cyprus, and that the necessary filings with the Department of Registrar of Companies be executed. RESOLVED: That [name] be and is hereby appointed as first director, and [name] as Secretary, each to serve until the next general meeting. RESOLVED: That the Company adopt the standard internal governance arrangements under the Companies Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (Ariadne Online System), Nicosia, Cyprus
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Ariadne online portal, select 'Name Reservation', search for availability against the Register of Companies. Submit up to three proposed English or Greek name variants, each ending with 'Limited' or 'Ltd' (or Greek equivalent). Pay the name reservation fee via government payment link. No notarization is required at this stage; retain the acknowledgement receipt.
required_dossiers: Copy of passport or identity card of the proposed director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any name is rejected as identical, confusing or offensive, submit revised alternatives within five business days through the same portal; a written clarification may be requested from the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constitution and Registered Office Letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel / notary; ultimate filing with Department of Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage qualified legal counsel to draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English in accordance with Companies Law Cap. 113 and Table A where applicable. Subscribers must sign each page before a witness; notarize signatures if requested or when using a foreign-incorporated subscriber. Obtain a signed consent letter from the Cyprus registered-office provider. Verify first directors and secretary consents to act.
required_dossiers: Consent of first directors and secretary (Form HE1 annex)
Notarized copy of each subscriber's passport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries defective clauses, counsel will issue drafting clarifications and execute amendments before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Application Submission and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (Ariadne online portal or in-person counter, Nicosia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form HE1 (Application for Registration of a Private Company as a Limited Company) and submit together with the executed constitutional documents via Ariadne or in person. Pay the statutory state filing fee online (approximately EUR 150 / USD 165). After review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, in paper or electronic form, evidencing the legal existence of the private limited company.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for incompleteness, rectify within 14 days using the Registrar's deficiency sheet. In case of substantive errors, withdraw and refile with a new submission fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Income Tax, VAT and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cyprus Tax Department (T.A.X.I.Snet portal) and Social Insurance Services (SIS web portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the T.A.X.I.Snet taxpayer portal, submit the corporate tax registration form (Form TD/E) and related registration information for income tax. If taxable turnover is expected to exceed the VAT registration threshold, also file the Form ME to obtain a VAT number. Separately register as an employer with Social Insurance Services for payroll and social contributions, using Form ISR1.
required_dossiers: Certified passport or identity card of each director
Registered office lease or utility bill
Form ME / VAT1 if VAT registration applies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If filing is incomplete, use the Tax Department's online rectification channel; re-submit missing certified translations within ten business days to avoid retroactive penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Statutory Registers and Corporate Governance File
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company directors and company secretary in consultation with the Registrar for any statutory filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a written resolution to ratify incorporation, adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, approve share allotment, fix the registered office, and appoint officers. Prepare and maintain statutory registers (directors, members, secretary, charges) under the Companies Law. Issue share certificates to subscribers and file any changes with the Registrar where required.
required_dossiers: Minutes of first board meeting (or written resolutions)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory registers are deficient or not timely filed, make corrective entries in the register and, where required, file Form HE3 (change in officers) within 14 days of the meeting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry (Industrial Licensing Division) – not applicable to software publishing; municipal business license may be required for physical office premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for electronic game publishing under ISIC 5820; optionally obtain a municipal business license from the district municipality for the registered office

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment (Cyprus)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – D2 office / non-industrial project category; no EIA required for low-impact digital services
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No hazardous discharges. Limited to municipal waste separation; office HVAC and electrical equipment must comply with EN 50419 for e-waste; no VOC emission limits applicable without manufacturing activities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by Cyprus Fire Service upon inspection of the registered office/leasehold; structural safety per municipal construction permits; workplace health and safety clearance under the Factories and Shops (Hours, Service and Inspection) Law and the Occupational Health and Safety Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Tax Department of the Republic of Cyprus, Ministry of Finance (Greek: Τμήμα Φορολογίας); primary electronic portal is the Tax Portal of Cyprus accessible at https://taxportal.cy, supplemented by the Ariadne integrated electronic filing platform for VAT, income tax, and EU recapitulative statements; customs and export-related procedures are administered by the Cyprus Customs Department (Τελωνείο) under the same Ministry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Cyprus Private Limited Company (HE77) is first incorporated at the Department of Registrar of Companies and Intellectual Property (D.R.C.I.P.). The registrar automatically notifies the Tax Department, which issues the Tax Identification Number (TIN/ΑΦΚ) for income tax and employer obligations. VAT registration is separate and compulsory on the Tax Portal: application must be made within 30 days from the date the company first engages in taxable transactions or exceeds the registration threshold. Non-resident foreign entities not incorporated in Cyprus but holding a Cyprus permanent establishment must obtain a TIN and VAT ID by filing Form TAX 011/VAT 101 through a Cyprus tax representative, attaching certified constitutional documents, board resolution appointing the representative, and proof of a fixed establishment address. Foreign founders may hold 100% of shares; no minimum subscribed capital is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation | Territorial_Scope | Non_Tax_Exempt_Zone. A Cyprus tax-resident private limited company is taxed at the entity level at the uniform 12.5% corporate income tax rate on worldwide income; a non-resident company is taxed only on Cyprus-source income attributable to a Cyprus permanent establishment. Cyprus applies a classical corporate system complemented by the participation exemption (intercorporate dividends and gains on disposal of shares are generally exempt) and territorial timing rules; no pass-through treatment or check-the-box entity classification exists under Cyprus domestic law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Cyprus has no US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections include: (i) group relief election for transfer of trading losses between companies holding at least 75% common ownership; (ii) Notional Interest Deduction election on new paid-in equity under section 9D of the Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002; (iii) 80% notional deduction election for qualifying intangible property (IP box) under section 9B, compatible with modified nexus rules; (iv) tonnage tax election for shipping; (v) election for deemed dividend distribution rules; (vi) election under section 2 of the Income Tax Law to deem a company managed and controlled abroad as non-resident where central management is effectively exercised outside Cyprus; (vii) VAT grouping election under the VAT Law 94(I)/2000; (viii) OSS and IOSS registration elections for intra-EU B2C distance sales and electronic services; and (ix) alignment elections under the hybrid mismatch provisions (ATAD) restricting double deduction and deduction/non-inclusion outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT/ΦΠΑ) under the Value Added Tax Law 94(I)/2000, as amended, transposing EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 15,600 annual taxable turnover of supplies in Cyprus through a fixed establishment; separate mandatory registration triggers include intra-Community acquisitions and intra-EU distance sales/e-services exceeding EUR 10,000 per calendar year (EU-wide threshold), in which case the supplier must either register in the member state of consumption or enrol in the OSS scheme; registration is effective from the first day of the month following the event that crosses the threshold, with optional registration available. For a hyper-casual games publisher monetising via AdMob (Google Ireland) and AppLovin, the operative trigger for EU consumer-facing electronic services is the EUR 10,000 OSS threshold; B2B supplies to EU counterparties are covered by reverse charge and EC Sales List reporting.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Cyprus imposes no mandatory domestic Continuous Transaction Control (CTC/real-time clearance) system, no fiscal stamping, and no mandatory B2B e-invoicing clearance. B2G e-invoicing is aligned with EU Directive 2014/55/EU via the Cypriot Peppol authority network on the Ariadne platform. Voluntary private-sector e-invoicing is permitted provided invoices satisfy structural and content rules of the VAT Law. All VAT returns (VAT 200) and EC Sales Lists must be filed electronically through Ariadne/Tax Portal. The European VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) proposal, once adopted EU-wide, will introduce mandatory structured e-invoicing and near-real-time transaction reporting in Cyprus only after the agreed EU implementation dates.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0%) is available under the Sixth Schedule of the Cyprus VAT Law for: (1) export of goods physically dispatched or transported outside the EU by or on behalf of the supplier; (2) intra-Community supplies to an EU customer holding a valid VAT identification number, subject to EC Sales List reporting; and (3) supplies of digital, software, online gaming, advertising inventory and telecommunication services to a customer established outside the EU, or to an EU non-taxable person where effective use and enjoyment is outside the EU, under Articles 58 and 59 of the VAT Directive. For hyper-casual game publishing, the ad-inventory supply to overseas platforms (US-based AppLovin, Google US) qualifies for zero-rating where the recipient is outside the EU; where the platform counterparty is EU-established (Google Ireland), the supply is taxable in the member state of the recipient via reverse charge and is excluded from Cyprus VAT. Substantiation requires contemporaneous evidence of the customer's non-EU status (VAT number validation, certificate of establishment, or Article 59 effective-use documentation), executed contracts, and platform payout statements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Cyprus Customs Export Declaration: Single Administrative Document (SAD/EU SAD) lodged electronically through the Ariadne customs e-system for any physical goods; for digital service exports, the functional equivalent is the executed digital service agreement, delivery/usage logs, and analytics evidence from AdMob/AppLovin platforms

Bill of Lading / Air Waybill: transport document evidencing physical dispatch from Cyprus for goods; for offshore digital services, the equivalent evidence is the published app store distribution record and IP licensing delivery acceptance

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC): issued by the Cyprus banking institution through which the foreign exchange proceeds of the export are repatriated, proving actual receipt of settlement from abroad

VAT compliance bundle: valid EU VAT numbers of EU platform customers with VIES validation reports, periodic EC Sales List (Recap Statement), and OSS reference numbers where the intra-EU B2C threshold is exceeded
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Tax Department and Cyprus Customs may re-audit zero-rated exports retrospectively within the standard 5-year limitation period, extended to 10 years in cases of fraudulent conduct. Penalties include: (i) reassessment of the export supplies at the standard 19% VAT with reversal of any claimed input VAT credit (clawback); (ii) administrative fines up to EUR 500 per non-compliance event and monthly interest of 1% on unpaid tax; (iii) additional penalties up to 50% of the tax under-assessed where negligence is proven; (iv) criminal liability for tax evasion and fraud, punishable on indictment by imprisonment of up to 3 years and/or unlimited fines; (v) publication of the taxpayer in the Tax Department's list of non-compliant/uncooperative taxpayers; and (vi) retrospective cancellation of zero-rating where the exporter fails to produce the customs export declaration, transport documentation, or Inward Remittance Certificate, or where goods are diverted back into the local market.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility under the EU capital movement regime; Cyprus adopted the euro on 1 January 2008. There are no exchange-control restrictions on current-account or capital-account transactions for EU or non-EU residents, subject to anti-money-laundering, sanctions screening, and Central Bank of Cyprus balance-of-payments statistical reporting. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, and intercompany loan repayment are unrestricted and, for non-resident corporate shareholders, generally free of Cypriot withholding tax, provided the receiving bank's KYC and source-of-funds protocols are satisfied.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Cyprus abolished statutory exchange controls upon EU accession and Eurozone entry; there is no mandatory export-proceeds surrender, repatriation timeline, or forced conversion ratio. A Cyprus resident company may retain digital advertising export receipts in any convertible currency, but the transactions must be identifiable against the underlying ad-network contracts and reported to the Central Bank of Cyprus by the servicing commercial bank through the standard balance-of-payments reporting framework.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability rating: High for treasury concentration, operational settlement, and low-value cross-border disbursements, with strict legal guardrails. A Cyprus private limited company may open accounts with Central Bank of Cyprus-regulated EMIs established in Cyprus or with EEA-licensed EMIs validly passporting into Cyprus, such as Revolut Business or MisterTango. These EMIs cannot serve as full credit-institution substitutes; they are not permitted for large-ticket capital escrow or commercial-lending facilities, and they remain subject to the same AML, sanctions, and UBO-disclosure standards as regulated banks. Offshore non-EEA EMIs are generally not viable as primary clearing accounts in Cyprus, since the Central Bank of Cyprus expects significant cross-border flows to settle through domestic banks or duly passporting EEA institutions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal statutory requirement that all directors appear physically in Cyprus. In practice, leading Cypriot banks require at least one authorised director or ultimate beneficial owner to attend an in-person account-opening interview, either at the bank's branch or before a local notary/approved external lawyer, while remote video-identity verification may be accepted for additional signatories. Remote account opening is permitted for low-risk corporate structures if the corporate pack is notarised and apostilled, UBO identities are verified through BCMS or an equivalent EU-compliant KYC system, and a physical visit to Cyprus is completed for at least one primary representative. Banks will otherwise devolve to enhanced due diligence and may reject the application if physical substance cannot be evidenced.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity third-party receipts from global ad networks (Google AdMob, AppLovin) into a newly incorporated Cypriot entity without local operational history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed publisher agreements for each ad network; platform dashboard statements for the last 3 to 6 monetisation cycles; monthly earnings reconciliation reports; board resolution establishing treasury control procedure; corporate bank reference from an existing partner/adequate institution; and legal opinion confirming the games are ad-supported, non-gambling software (ISIC 5820).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO structure with no full-time director presence in Cyprus, raising 'tax-resident shell' and 'beneficial-ownership opacity' concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation and memorandum/articles; certified register of shareholders and directors; Cyprus Registrar beneficial-ownership filing confirmation; notarised UBO register and identity documentation; lease agreement or serviced-office licence; local director's professional CV and tax residency certificate; group organogram; source-of-wealth statement supported by bank transaction profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business description mistakenly classified as online gaming, gambling, or micro-transaction valueless consumer spending, which exceeds the bank's low-risk digital-media appetite.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provenance memorandum aligning ISIC 5820 / NAICS 511210; non-gambling compliance letter from Cypriot legal counsel; then-current terms of service and end-user licence agreement; GDPR compliance and Data Protection Officer appointment; privacy notification mechanisms; and an advertising-monetisation model narrative showing zero real-money wagering or paid prize mechanics.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border shareholder capital injection from a non-EEA jurisdiction for an entity with nominal physical substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed equity subscription agreement or intercompany loan agreement; board minutes authorising the injection and treasury allocation; share-allotment forms (HE32/HE08 as applicable) and updated UBO register; remitting bank's customer-due-diligence confirmation; source-of-funds documents (salary, dividend, disposal, or wealth accumulation records); and a one-page economic-substance rationale proving the funds will be deployed inside the Cypriot company's operational treasury.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed through SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA credit transfer when originating in an SEPA jurisdiction) with an unambiguous purpose classification. For equity contributions, the instruction must quote 'Capital subscription / paid-in capital'; for shareholder loans, it must cite the intercompany loan agreement and use the standard purpose code for intercompany financing. The remitting bank must forward the underlying contract and source-of-funds confirmation so the receiving Cypriot bank can complete BOP reporting to the Central Bank of Cyprus. The company should maintain the full corporate-authorisation chain — board minutes, share allotment forms, updated UBO declaration, and any relevant CRS/FATCA certificates — for at least five years and must inform the relationship manager before the value date for pre-clearance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For high-value cross-border trade settlements, the default clearing rail is SWIFT MT103, supplemented by MT202 for interbank positioning, with invoice numbers, contract references, and anti-money-laundering narrative codes attached. Within the EEA, SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant (SCT Inst) are used for low-value recurring payouts to EU developers, ad-agencies, and service providers. For procurement of digital advertising or monetisation infrastructure, standard bank wires remain sufficient; commercial letters of credit and standby letters of credit are permissible but are generally reserved for high-value, asset-backed or documentary transactions where the supplier requires bank-risk mitigation. The treasury should leverage host-to-host SWIFT/EBICS connectivity to align outgoing payment flows with the daily settlement schedules of AstroPay/AdMob/AppLovin payouts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla foreign exchange forwards (currency forwards) with fixed delivery date and price
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where physical USD/EUR delivery is impractical or restricted by counterparty policy
Foreign exchange swaps (tom-next, spot-next, and forward-dated) for liquidity and rolling-maturity management
Cross-currency swaps (EURLIB vs SOFR) for long-term balance-sheet hedging
European-style FX options (call/put) purchased on an OTC basis, subject to MiFID II/EMIR suitability and ISDA documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (HE32) – confirmation of registered details, members, and share capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cyprus Department of Registrar of Companies (DRoC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days of the company's annual incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EUR 30 for the first month and EUR 30 per subsequent month, capped at EUR 300; continued default may lead to administrative strike-off and dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements (where statutory audit applies) filed with the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cyprus Department of Registrar of Companies (DRoC) via the PSC/beneficial ownership filing module
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 months from the end of the financial year, subject to a maximum extension aligned with the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal liability for directors; civil late filing fees; persistent non-compliance triggers automatic strike-off and application by the Registrar for dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual report of the directors and auditor's report submission for companies under audit obligation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in general meeting; notice to Registrar of Companies where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting must be held within 18 months of incorporation and thereafter no more than 15 months apart
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Summary penalties under the Companies Law, Cap. 113; failure to hold AGM is an offence; court direction available to order a meeting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register annual confirmation (UBO Declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cyprus Registrar of Companies – Beneficial Ownership Register (under AML Law 188(I)/2007 as amended)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change; annual confirmation no later than 60 days from the date of change or upon each calendar-year review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 200 per non-compliance event and criminal sanctions; directors may be personally fined for failure to update the register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form TD4.1 including audited financial statements where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 December of the year following the tax year (i.e., tax year 2024 return due by 31 December 2025); extensions available for audited companies until 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EUR 100; further penalties of 5% of tax payable for each month of delay up to 50%; potential tax assessment based on estimated chargeable income

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT return (Form 508) annual/periodic where registration threshold exceeded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of each VAT period; annual listing return (Form ELGL 517) due by 31 December following the end of the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Financial penalties up to 10% of the VAT due; interest charged at statutory rate; criminal sanctions for willful evasion in severe cases

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Social Insurance Fund employer contribution declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Employer contribution returns and payments due monthly on or before the last day of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest at statutory rates; administrative fines and entitlement loss for employees' contributory benefits

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit mandatory for all Cyprus private limited companies except small companies meeting two of the following criteria for the relevant financial year: total assets not exceeding EUR 4,000,000; turnover not exceeding EUR 8,000,000; or average number of employees not exceeding 50; such exempt companies may still require audit by order of members holding 10% of share capital or under consolidated group requirements; ISIC 5820 digital gaming entities commonly exceed the asset threshold and must file audited accounts
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the EU; Cyprus FRS (based on IFRS for SME) permitted for certain small private entities; Companies Law Cap. 113 requires true and fair view in accordance with applicable accounting standards

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Cyprus Registrar of Companies mandates a Beneficial Ownership Register; companies registered before 2024 must confirm beneficial ownership details annually within 30 days after each change and no later than 60 days from any triggering event; any shareholding transfer resulting in a change of beneficial ownership requires immediate filing of the updated register and notification to the Registrar within 30 days; electronically transmitted one-time confirmation for pre-existing entities has been replaced by an ongoing obligation to maintain and submit each distinct alteration; deadlines run from the occurrence of the change, not the calendar year-end

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 – USD 1,800 per annum for registered office, corporate secretarial, and appointed director services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 – USD 5,000 per annum for a low-complexity hyper-casual gaming entity with a single legal entity and intercompany transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% flat corporate income tax rate under the Cyprus Income Tax Law (L.118(I)/2002, as amended).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cyprus IP Box: 80% exemption on qualifying intangible-asset profits yields a 2.5% effective tax rate, subject to the OECD nexus ratio. Notional Interest Deduction (NID) on new equity reduces effective tax further. Foreign dividend and foreign permanent establishment profit exemptions apply if the company demonstrates adequate substance and satisfies anti-abuse conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 - Cyprus Corporate Income Tax Return, filed electronically through the Taxisnet portal (https://taxisnet.net.cy).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 must be filed within six months after the end of the tax year; for a calendar year-end company, the statutory deadline is 30 June of the following year. Extensions may be granted only at the discretion of the Tax Commissioner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal name, Companies Registry Number (HE77 format), Tax Identification Code (TIC), registered address, fiscal year end and main activity code (ISIC 5820).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not need a Cyprus TIC; enter the Cyprus entity's TIC and disclose the UBO country in the supplementary details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Turnover and gross receipts: total gross revenue from hyper-casual game publishing, including AdMob, AppLovin and other ad-network payouts, before deducting platform fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide turnover only if central management and control is exercised in Cyprus. Otherwise report Cyprus-source income only and attach treaty source allocators.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and operating expenses: user acquisition spend, App Store/Google Play commissions, SDK licensing costs, sub-contractor costs and administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses wholly and exclusively incurred in generating Cyprus-taxable income. Related-party charges require contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back list: disallowable expenses such as non-business entertainment, penalties, notional interest not paid, and artificial or excessive related-party management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign holding-company charges imposed on the Cyprus Ltd must prove actual intra-group benefit and be priced on an arm's length basis; otherwise they are rigidly disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reliefs and deductions: IP Box deduction, Notional Interest Deduction, double tax treaty relief and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: IP Box calculations require a separate supporting schedule showing qualifying intangible assets and core income-generating activities performed in Cyprus. Attach the tax residence certificate (TRC) for overseas credit claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation: final taxable profit multiplied by 12.5%, reduced by advance tax instalments and provisional tax, resulting in net tax payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any remaining tax must be settled through Taxisnet. No dividend withholding tax is deducted when profits are later distributed to non-residents.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a fixed penalty of EUR 100 plus EUR 50 for each month of continued default, capped at EUR 500. Incorrect returns attract adjustment penalties of EUR 200 up to EUR 1,000. Late payment of tax carries statutory interest at 2% per annum over the Central Bank of Cyprus Treasury bill rate, plus an additional surcharge up to 5% on the unpaid amount for each quarter, capped at 30%, and criminal liability may add a fine of EUR 5,000 and/or imprisonment up to three years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR2 - Provisional Tax Return, filed electronically via the Taxisnet system for the purpose of self-assessed advance tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual with three instalments within the tax year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Provisional tax instalments are due on 1 August, 31 December, and 31 March following the tax year. The IR2 estimate itself must be submitted by 31 March of the tax year following the close of the year, or earlier if the taxpayer anticipates a liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated taxable profit for the current tax year before reliefs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Cyprus Ltd carries on business only through a foreign permanent establishment, report only Cyprus-source allocable profit and attach a computation note.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated corporate tax payable at 12.5% on the estimated taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the prior final assessment as a safe baseline; over- or under-estimates by more than 5% of actual liability trigger interest unless reasonable cause is shown.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Voluntary excess instalment threshold: an optional declaration to increase instalment payments to avoid late-payment penalties following uncertain year-end adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders often elect a conservative higher estimate to protect against the 5% quarterly surcharge where the final tax amount is uncertain.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file IR2 or to pay instalments triggers an immediate surcharge of 5% on the unpaid amount and interest at 2% above the official Central Bank rate. Repeated non-compliance subjects the company's directors to a criminal penalty of up to EUR 5,000 and direct liability for the withheld amount.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Cyprus law imposes no withholding tax on dividends distributed by a Cyprus resident company to its shareholders, whether resident or non-resident. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive further confirms a 0% WHT for qualifying EU corporate parents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because the domestic dividend withholding tax rate is zero, no DTA relief application is normally necessary for dividend distributions. If a DTA rate claim is ever needed for non-dividend income (interest or royalties), the non-resident recipient must provide a valid Cyprus Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign competent authority and submit the official Cyprus DTA relief application form (Form DTA-1) to the Cyprus Tax Department through the payer before the payment is made. The application must be filed within three years of the end of the tax year, and the payer must retain the TRC and application approval for audit purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents for game software copyrights, mobile game licences and SDKs are generally exempt from Cyprus withholding tax under domestic law, provided the non-resident derives the income without a Cyprus permanent establishment. Interest paid to non-residents is likewise exempt from withholding tax. Under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, related companies with at least 25% direct ownership may benefit from a mandatory 0% withholding rate. Where a Cypriot permanent establishment exists, Cyprus retains the right to tax the royalty or interest income on a net basis at 12.5%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000 aggregate annual value of controlled goods and services transactions; EUR 250,000 for controlled financing and royalty transactions. The Cyprus Tax Department requires contemporaneous Local File documentation when these thresholds are exceeded, and requests submission within a 30-day notice.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Cyprus applies an OECD/G20 BEPS-aligned economic substance doctrine. For a Cyprus Ltd to retain tax residence and the 12.5% preferential rate, the board of directors must exercise genuine management and control in Cyprus, and the company must have adequate personnel, premises and risk control with respect to its hyper-casual gaming activities. The Cyprus Tax Department will deny the IP Box and treaty residence benefits where substance is artificial. There is no separate ESR notification regime for gaming companies, but the 2019 Tax Department circular and the UBO register require supporting evidence of real business activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-reporting AdMob and AppLovin ad payouts by shifting gross revenue to foreign payment processors, or inflating user-acquisition costs using fictitious invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Section 8 of the Assessment and Collection of Taxes Law (Law 4/1979) and Income Tax Law L.118(I)/2002, the Tax Commissioner may add up to 100% of the evaded tax together with annual interest, impose a criminal fine of up to EUR 5,000, and imprison the responsible persons for up to three years. The courts may also require the restitution of all tax plus compound interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who knowingly sign false IR4 returns are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and civil restitution. Travel bans, port arrest orders and disqualification from being directors for up to five years may be imposed, in addition to criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Cyprus Ltd as a flow-through vehicle for game monetization while all board meetings, key decision-making and game management remain abroad, with no real office or employees in Cyprus.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Cyprus tax residence test (Income Tax Law section 2), the company may be treated as non-resident and lose the 12.5% corporate rate; all previously claimed exemptions are withdrawn. EU CFC rules and the Cyprus CFC provision in section 38A may attribute profits to the foreign parent. The company may also be struck off under the Companies Law for failing to have a registered office and registered agent, attracting cancellation of tax incentives and treaty reliefs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who declare a false Cyprus tax residence certificate face disqualification orders and civil liability for the resulting tax deficiency. If the shell entity is used for fraudulent insolvency or tax evasion, courts pierce the corporate veil and impose personal restitution, travel bans and imprisonment up to three years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file accurate UBO declarations with the Cyprus Registrar of Companies, or processing large volumes of ad-net revenue without verifying the source of funds of founders and payment beneficiaries, or transacting with sanctioned publishers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Cyprus AML Law (L.188(I)/2007) as amended and the UBO Law (L.88(I)/2019), the Registrar may impose administrative fines of up to EUR 100,000, daily default fines of EUR 100, and refer the case to MOKAS for asset freezing orders. Conviction for money laundering carries imprisonment up to five years and fines up to EUR 200,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly accepting proceeds of crime through payment rails are personally criminally liable. The court may order civil restitution of laundered amounts, issue international travel bans, prohibit banking operations, and, in serious cases, dissolve the company and hold directors personally responsible for all claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging above-market user-acquisition or licensing fees to a related foreign distributor, performing no functional analysis, and failing to prepare a Cyprus Local File despite related-party turnover exceeding EUR 750,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Cyprus transfer pricing rules aligned with OECD guidelines and section 68(2) of the Income Tax Law, the Tax Commissioner may adjust taxable profits to the arm's length level, impose additional tax of up to 25% of the adjusted amount, and levy interest and penalties of 5% to 10% on the under-declared tax. A specific administrative fine of up to EUR 30,000 applies for failure to produce contemporaneous TP records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly implement TP schemes with no economic substance may be held jointly and severally liable for the adjustment, additional tax and penalties. If the scheme is found to be a fraudulent concealment of profit, criminal prosecution may lead to imprisonment up to three years and a travel ban pending recovery of the tax debt.
